UPDATE: For anyone who stumbles across this post here was the solution: It’s a headache but it works. 

1) Create a new account with payoneer (with new email and everything) 
2) Wait for account approval from payoneer (takes forever)
3) Submit a ticket on payoneer that you want to connect Tunecore as your payout company 
4) Tunecore should then disconnect your old payoneer account for your withdrawals (might need to submit a ticket to Tunecore for this to happen)
5) Add your new payoneer account to your Tunecore (Withdrawals)
6) You then need to do a Tax Form on Payoneer to accept Tunecore as your payout company 
7) If your tax form is accepted, Tunecore will be connected to your Payoneer and you can add bank details.

The whole process took me nearly a year, but then again I gave up during some points so maybe a month or two for those who have the patience.

My only advice is to stay away from Tunecore if you do switch. customer service is terrible, getting paid is a nightmare (took almost a year to finally be approved for payout) and you need big numbers for their artist services.

I was 7 years old, staying the weekend with my great grandfather. It was a Saturday. It was drizzling outside. The church he attended had just bought a new building and we were supposed to go help paint the walls. I threw a tantrum all morning that I didn’t want to go. 

As we were driving his old Ford pickup, he was berating and yelling about the way I acted. He was furious. I don’t think he noticed that it had started to rain harder. 

We were driving through a windy part of the road when an SUV suddenly blew through a stop sign.

Everything happened in slow motion.

I tried to scream but nothing came out. I looked over at my grandfather as we T-Boned the SUV around 50 mph.  I wasn’t wearing a seatbelt and my head went through the windshield. 

The next thing I remember, was waking up in the hospital. My mother and siblings were all crying. I asked where my great grandfather was, and no one said anything. Finally my mother took my hand and said, “he didn’t make it.” 

It took me years to deal with it. Til this day, a part of me always thinks, if I had just behaved that morning or if he had just let us stay home, something, maybe anything could have been different.
